name: Mission Basilica of San Diego de Alcalá
history: Founded by St. Junípero Serra on 16 July 1769, this was the first of the Alta California missions, on land long home to the Kumeyaay people. The first mission was burned in an uprising in 1775, in which Father Luis Jayme was killed; he is honoured as California's first Christian martyr. The present church, built in the early 1800s, is the fifth on the site.
arch: Whitewashed adobe and plaster with a tall campanario (bell wall) beside the church, the classic silhouette of the California missions.
features: Father Luis Jayme is buried beneath the chancel floor.
The mission is California Historical Landmark #242.

look.d: The stepped bell wall holds the mission's bells in open arches instead of a tower.
The present church is the fifth to stand on this spot.

fun: The mission marks the starting point of El Camino Real in Alta California.
journal: The first mission of Alta California. The bells hang in the open, and a martyr rests under the floor.

quiz.q: Who was California's first Christian martyr, buried here?
